tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

tools.name: read_text_file
tools.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. tools.name: read_media_file
tools.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: read_multiple_files

tools.name: write_file

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: create_directory

tools.name: list_directory_with_sizes

This tool is useful for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works with

tools.name: directory_tree
tools.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty). The output is formatted with 2-space indenta

tools.name: move_file

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: list_allowed_directories
tools.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

tools.name: create_relations

tools.description: Compresses a single file using gzip compression. Depending upon the selected output type, returns either the compressed data as a gzipped resource or a resource link, allowing it to be downloaded in a subsequent request: during the current session for a 2025-era client, or for ten minutes at a minte

tools.name: trigger-list-changed
tools.description: Sends a notifications/<list>/list_changed for the tool, prompt or resource list. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream that asked for that list; a 2025-era client receives it unsolicited.

tools.name: trigger-log-messages
tools.description: Sends one log message at each logging level during the call. On protocol version 2026-07-28 only the messages at or above the level the request names in _meta (io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel) are sent, and none if it names no level; a 2025-era client gets those at or above the level it set with lo

tools.name: trigger-long-running-operation
tools.description: Demonstrates a long running operation with progress updates.

tools.name: trigger-resource-update
tools.description: Sends a notifications/resources/updated for a resource URI. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream whose resourceSubscriptions name the URI; a 2025-era client receives it once it has called resources/subscribe for the URI.

tools.name: toggle-simulated-logging
tools.description: Toggles simulated, random-leveled logging on or off. Deprecated: 2025-era clients only, since protocol version 2026-07-28 removes logging/setLevel; use trigger-log-messages with a per-request log level instead.

tools.name: toggle-subscriber-updates
tools.description: Toggles simulated resource subscription updates on or off. Deprecated: 2025-era clients only, since protocol version 2026-07-28 removes resources/subscribe; use trigger-resource-update with a subscriptions/listen stream instead.
